source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix route #[post("/collections/{collection_name}/points/query/batch")] query_points_batch (src/actix/api/query_api.rs:110, takes Json<QueryRequestBatch> — serde deserialization happens in the JSON extractor) -> QueryRequestBatch.searches: Vec<QueryRequest> (schema.rs:604) -> QueryRequest.internal (flattened QueryRequestInternal, schema.rs:596) -> QueryRequestInternal.query: Option<QueryInterface> (schema.rs:559) -> QueryInterface #[serde(untagged)] Nearest(VectorInput)|Query(Query) (schema.rs:615) -> Query #[serde(untagged)] with Nearest declared FIRST, OrderBy fifth (schema.rs:624). Rust serde untagged deserialization tries variants in declaration order and takes the first that succeeds; the struct variants (NearestQuery{nearest, mmr}, etc.) carry NO #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] (zero occurrences in schema.rs), so an object {"nearest": [...], "order_by": {...}} deserializes successfully as NearestQuery with the order_by key silently ignored — first-match-wins key discard. Downstream, From<QueryInterface> for Query (conversions.rs:129) and convert_query_request_from_rest (query_requests_rest.rs:96) operate on the already-resolved variant, and the Validate impl (validate.rs:33-48) validates only the chosen variant — no layer anywhere checks oneOf exclusivity or detects the discarded key.
source_grounding.outcome_note: The contract-required oneOf-exclusivity validation (reject a query object matching more than one variant) is absent from the entire deserialization-to-execution path; the observed 200-with-nearest-fingerprint behavior is exactly what the untagged first-match + unknown-field-ignoring mechanism produces. NOT marked by_design_in_source: the source contains no explicit intent evidence for dual-key tolerance (the #[serde(expecting)] attribute at schema.rs:616 only shapes the error message when ALL variants fail; the variant doc-comments describe single-variant semantics only) — per the v3.4 tightened rule, unannotated silent behavior is forbidden from being marked by_design_in_source. The Fern API reference rendering the union as undiscriminatedUnion (anyOf-style, no exclusivity promise) is recorded for the auditor as doc-side context.
